- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) or trending negative, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp price spikes (≥10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 5–10 day horizons.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and prices are trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 7–14 day horizons.
- Mean reversion is stronger in low-sentiment periods; if 3–5 consecutive days show downward drift, forecast should trend lower by 1–3% per day.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates volatility in high-sentiment periods; add 1–3% upward bias if sentiment >0.6 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment drops sharply after a peak, model fails to adjust; check for lagged correction: if sentiment drops >0.2 from prior day, reduce forecast by 1–4% for next 3 days.
